k3s.invariant: MEASURED, not read: a `server --disable-agent` binds *:https-listen-port AND 127.0.0.1:port+1 as a PAIR, and binds NOTHING on --advertise-port in steady state; /cacerts answers 200 on the listen port and 401 on the advertise port, so a node dialing the advertise port loops on 'failed to get CA certs'. Two --disable-agent servers DID run concurrently on one host, each with its own kine and store. The server still runs the agent bootstrap and so needs /etc/rancher/node/password readable and writable -- NOT under --data-dir, no flag moves it -- but its VALUE is never checked, because no node registers through it and the k3s-<node> Secret that would disagree is never created. An AGENT cannot share a host: 127.0.0.1:6444 collides FATALLY, one containerd socket, one flannel.1, one IPAM pool, one set of KUBE-* chains, and it is fatal as a non-root user ('agent requires additional privilege if not run with --rootless').

kcp.invariant: MUST run --feature-gates=WorkspaceMounts=true. With the gate off, installWorkspaceMountsScheduler returns early (kcp/pkg/server/controllers.go:733-737) and EVERY TENANT'S MOUNTED API SILENTLY STOPS BEING SERVED -- objects survive, the mount does not.

kine.invariant: kine IS the store, and k3s must DIAL it rather than consume its bucket: an empty --datastore-endpoint makes k3s start its own sqlite and a BRAND-NEW cluster, silently. It also ships no prebuilt release for every target, so CGO_ENABLED=1 is part of the recipe rather than an optimisation.

rustfs.invariant: NO writable second instance, ever. t4's fence is an S3 conditional write INSIDE the bucket, so a writable replica is a split brain by construction (ADR 0026 R15).

embedded-postgres.version: the host's own binaries: initdb/postgres/psql on PATH, PostgreSQL 18.x
embedded-postgres.how: exec'd directly; the org's ferrugstrange/embedded-postgres launcher is used by an experiment only and is NOT linked into this module
embedded-postgres.invariant: THE PORT IS REQUIRED AND NEVER DEFAULTED: a default is ADR 0026's byte-identical DSN, so PostgresSpec.Port is refused when zero. postgres ALSO refuses to run as root ('initdb: error: cannot be run as root') while a k3s agent requires root, so a host that runs the store cannot run a local-process node -- which is why the node substrate is a VM. The store binds 127.0.0.1 ONLY and its pg_hba admits 127.0.0.1/32: the only client is kine, a child of the same process group.

openbao.invariant: 2.6.2 has NO DEFAULT secret/ MOUNT, and the ESO SecretStore path is hardcoded to secret. Its config file is generated per cluster by this repo (see clusterstack) rather than shipped: the listener is loopback on the cluster's leased port, because the process group is gateway-side.

external-secrets.how: the control-plane image copies /usr/bin/external-secrets (the upstream image's /bin is a link to usr/bin) out of the digest-pinned upstream image to /usr/local/bin/external-secrets, and fetches the same release's external-secrets.yaml to /opt/socialweb/eso/external-secrets.yaml, checked against bundleSha256 (deploy/control-plane-container/Dockerfile carries the same three values and a test holds them equal). The provider runs it per cluster in the process group, beside the control plane, and installs the bundle's CRDs, ClusterRoles and validating-webhook registration into the tenant (internal/eso, internal/clusterprovider/externalsecrets.go); internal/esovault applies the cluster's own ClusterSecretStore and ExternalSecret over the placeholders in deploy/eso
external-secrets.measured: 2026-10-07: TestAZeroNodeMarketClusterSyncsAnExternalSecretFromItsOwnVaultWithNoESOPodInTheTenant PASS -- a market-dialled cluster at zero nodes reached Ready with the pair in its group in 22.68 s, the tenant apiserver called the webhook on https://127.0.0.1:<leased> (an ExternalSecret with no data was denied by validate.externalsecret.external-secrets.io), and users/openbao-demo carried the vault's value 500 ms after the store was applied, with no External Secrets pod or Deployment in the tenant
external-secrets.invariant: The controller and its webhook are TWO processes of one pinned binary, per cluster, in the cluster's process group after the cloud controller manager, and the tenant holds only the bundle's 25 CRDs and 4 ClusterRoles, a ClusterRoleBinding of external-secrets-controller to the group system:socialweb:external-secrets, and the two ValidatingWebhookConfigurations re-registered by URL. Every other bundle object (3 Deployments, 3 ServiceAccounts, the webhook Service and Secret, the cert-controller's ClusterRole and both upstream ClusterRoleBindings, the leader-election Role and RoleBinding) is RETIRED: deleted at every spawn, because a binding to a ServiceAccount nothing runs as is one a tenant who creates that ServiceAccount inherits. The upstream defaults (:8080 metrics, :8082 controller health, :8081 webhook health, 10250 webhook) are one set for the host, so each cluster leases its own: controller health and webhook health bind 127.0.0.1, metrics are off (--metrics-addr=0), leader election is off (one process group per cluster is already the singleton). The webhook's --port has no host flag and binds every interface (measured: 'Serving webhook server' with host empty); it serves only admission answers under a CA the provider mints per cluster. The store authenticates with OpenBao CERT auth against the cluster vault's LOOPBACK listener, which every substrate reaches because the controller is a process in the same container, so it syncs at zero nodes. The webhook registrations stay failurePolicy Ignore: the pair is not restarted when it dies (the cloud controller manager is not either), and a dead webhook under Fail would refuse even the provider's own store writes and deletes.

apimachinery.invariant: the only version pinned in TRACKED CODE, and it is pinned by the module system rather than by this file.

our-crds.invariant: v1alpha1 means NO COMPATIBILITY PROMISE, which is true of the promise and FALSE OF THE COST: in kcp a schema cannot be changed in place, and identityHash DETERMINES THE ETCD PREFIX -- change it and every stored object reads from an EMPTY PREFIX. MEASURED in addition: APIResourceSchema.spec is IMMUTABLE, so an added enum or field is a NEW schema revision (v1alpha1-<Revision>.<plural>.<group>, Revision in api/v1alpha1/resources.go, guarded by deploy/apiresourceschema-revisions.json) and the exports must be re-pointed; the identity hash survives a re-point, and MEASURED on kcp v0.33.0 (internal/apigen live upgrade proof) the re-point DOES reach an already-bound APIBinding: its boundResources move to the new schema within seconds and fields the old schema pruned then persist. And `Cluster` and `Node` ride ONE export, `clusters`, because a WorkspaceType's defaultAPIBindings names an export and the test that guards it requires every entry to equal that export's name. A phase written through the main resource is DISCARDED when the schema declares a status subresource -- the node provider's writes must go through /status.

t4.invariant: t4 is NOT a separate binary and has NO PINNED VERSION ANYWHERE -- it is a kine backend selected by endpoint scheme, so pinning kine pins t4. Its fence is an S3 CONDITIONAL WRITE INSIDE THE BUCKET, which is why a WRITABLE SECOND rustfs is a split brain by construction and failover must never fail back (ADR 0026 R15). Note single-node t4 NEVER TOUCHES THE LEADER LOCK (node.go:657 -- no peer address means roleSingle), so the multi-node shape is a different exercise.

one-node-per-host.how: a measured constraint, not a component
one-node-per-host.invariant: A k3s AGENT cannot share a host with another: 127.0.0.1:6444 binds FATALLY and the loser is served the other cluster's CA; one /run/k3s/containerd/containerd.sock (hardcoded, --data-dir moves 'root' only, measured cross-contamination: cluster A's containerd served RunPodSandbox for cluster B's pods), one flannel.1 whose NAME is not redirectable and whose reconfiguration panicked agent A (vxlan_network.go:217), one 8472/udp socket, one /run/flannel/subnet.env, one IPAM pool, one set of KUBE-* iptables chains, /var/lib/kubelet/pod-resources. All four candidate fixes were refuted. Control planes have no such limit: N servers per host, ports leased.
